title: Whose is this?
goal: Point at things, ask who owns them, and use 的 — one character that does the work of "'s", "of", "who/which", and every long description.
bekal: tell 這 from 那 and use them with measure words
use 的 for possession — and know when to leave it out
ask questions with 誰, 什麼, 哪 without changing the word order

dialogs.title: 對話 — 教室裡的雨傘
dialogs.intro: An afternoon downpour in Taipei. Budi finds an umbrella left behind on a classroom bench.

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.id: That's an umbrella. It rains a lot in Taipei.
lines.literal: that — is — rain-umbrella — (you know). Taipei — often-often — fall-rain.

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.text: [我|Wǒ][不知道|bù zhīdào]。[不是|Bú shì][我的|wǒ de]。
lines.id: I don't know. It's not mine.
lines.literal: I — not — know. not — is — I — 's.

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [那|Nà][那個|nà ge][背包|bēibāo][呢|ne]？[也|Yě][不是|bú shì][你的|nǐ de][嗎|ma]？
lines.id: What about that backpack? Not yours either?
lines.literal: then — that — (measure word) — back-bag — (what about)? also — not — is — you — 's — (question)?

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.text: [那個|Nà ge][是|shì][阿明|Ā Míng][的|de]。[他|Tā][常常|chángcháng][忘東西|wàng dōngxi]。

lines.literal: that — (measure word) — is — A-Ming — 's. he — often-often — forget — east-west.

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [哈哈|Hāhā]！[那|Nà][雨傘|yǔsǎn][應該|yīnggāi][也是|yě shì][他的|tā de][吧|ba]？
lines.id: Haha! So the umbrella must be his too, right?
lines.literal: haha! then — umbrella — should — also — is — he — 's — (right)?

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.literal: have — possibility — (you know). we — ask-ask — him.

lines.speaker: 布迪:
lines.text: [等一下|Děng yíxià]，[這|zhè][是|shì][我的|wǒ de][手機|shǒujī][嗎|ma]？
lines.id: Hey, wait — is this my phone?
lines.literal: wait — a-moment, this — is — I — 's — hand-machine — (question)?

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.text: [你的|Nǐ de][手機|shǒujī][在|zài][你|nǐ][手上|shǒu shàng][啦|la]！

lines.literal: you — 's — phone — is-at — you — hand — on — (la)!

lines.id: Oh… sorry. I'm so tired today.
lines.literal: ah… not — good — meaning. I — today — very — tired.

lines.speaker: 小美:
lines.text: [沒關係|Méi guānxi]。[你|Nǐ][的|de][中文|Zhōngwén][課|kè][幾點|jǐ diǎn]？

lines.literal: not — have — relation. you — 's — Chinese — class — how-many — o'clock?

lines.text: [三點|Sān diǎn]。[還有|Hái yǒu][二十|èrshí][分鐘|fēnzhōng]。

lines.id: Then hurry up! Leave the umbrella here for now.

notes: **這 (*zhè*, this) and 那 (*nà*, that)** work just like in English. ⚠️ The difference: when a noun follows, **a measure word must sit in between**. 這**個**背包, 那**把**雨傘 — not 這背包.

⚠️ **那 does two jobs.** As a pointer it means "that"; at the **start of a sentence** it means "then", "in that case". *那我們走吧！* — "Let's go, then!" Context always tells them apart, and the second use turns up in almost every conversation.
**吧 (*ba*) softens a sentence into a suggestion or a guess.** *走吧！* "let's go!" *是他的吧？* "it's his, right?" It is never used for a real question — if you genuinely don't know, use 嗎.
**問問 and 等一下 show Mandarin's habit of softening verbs.** Doubling the verb (問問, 看看, 想想) or adding 一下 gives a sense of "just quickly, no pressure" — like "have a quick look" in English.
⚠️ **手機 = phone** (literally "hand machine"), and **東西 = thing, stuff** (literally "east west"). Two words you can't guess from their parts; learn them whole.

grammars.title: 的: one character, three jobs
body: **的** is the most frequent character in Mandarin, and it does three things that English handles in three different ways.

head: Job
Example
Meaning
rows: the friend who came from Tainan

after: The key is one sentence: **的 always stands right BEFORE the noun it describes**, and every description goes in front of it. Mandarin order is always **describer → 的 → described**. English does the same with short ones ("my book") but puts longer ones after the noun ("the friend *who came from Tainan*"); Mandarin never does.
⚠️ Practice reading from the end: 台南來的朋友 → start from 朋友 (friend), then go forward: the friend *who* came from Tainan. This reading-backwards habit will serve you all the way to B1.

grammars.title: ⚠️ When to leave 的 out
body: There is one important case where adding 的 actually sounds wrong: **very close relationships** — family, school, country, workplace. There 的 is dropped.
after: You can feel the reason: 的 marks ownership as something that **can change hands**. Your mother doesn't change hands, so marking her that way sounds like treating her as an object.
⚠️ This mistake won't stop people understanding you, but it is one of the quickest signs of a beginner. Fix it now while your vocabulary is still small.

sections.title: Question words: just swap them in place

blocks.text: Here is Mandarin's second gift, and it's a big one. To ask a question with a question word, **put the question word exactly where the answer will stand**. Nothing moves to the front as it does in English.

head: Question word
Pīnyīn
Meaning
Example
rows: 這是**什麼**？ What is this?
**哪**個是你的？ Which one is yours?
你在**哪裡**？ ⚠️ Taiwan uses 哪裡
你**什麼時候**去？ When are you going?
你**為什麼**不去？ Why aren't you going?
**怎麼**去？ How do you get there?

blocks.text: Compare: *他是誰？* and its answer *他是老師。* The word 誰 stands exactly where 老師 will stand. ⚠️ **Never add 嗎 to a sentence that already has a question word** — *你是誰嗎？* is wrong. One question marker per sentence is enough.

blocks.title: Lost property in Taiwan
items: **我的東西不見了。** *Wǒ de dōngxi bú jiàn le.* — I've lost my things.
**這是我的。** *Zhè shì wǒ de.* — This is mine.
**這不是我的。** *Zhè bú shì wǒ de.* — This isn't mine.
**失物招領處在哪裡？** *Shīwù zhāolǐng chù zài nǎlǐ?* — Where is the lost and found?
⚠️ Taiwan is famous as a place where lost things usually come back. The 捷運 and 便利商店 have procedures for it, and people really do hand in what they find.

sections.title: 這 and 那 with measure words

blocks.text: ⚠️ **那個 (*nà ge*) is also a filler word** while people think, just like "um…" or "you know…" in English: *那個…我想問一下。* You'll hear it many times in one conversation — don't be confused, it isn't pointing at anything.

exercises.prompt: Add 的 where needed; write ✗ where it must not be used.
Fill in the right question word: 誰, 什麼, 哪裡, 幾, or 多少.
Put the words in the right order.
items: 背包 / 是 / 阿明的 / 那個
媽媽 / 是 / 我 / 老師

answers: 這是什麼？ — 這把雨傘是誰的？ — 這不是我的。 — 我媽媽是印尼人。 — 哪個是你的？ — 我不知道。
誰 — 什麼 — 哪裡 — 幾 — 多少 — 哪
這是誰的？ — 這不是我的。 — 那是什麼？ — 那個背包是阿明的。 — 我媽媽是老師。
